candidates.original_title: The Marley hypothesis: Denial of racism reflects ignorance of history
candidates.description: Study 1 tested whether White students would have less knowledge of historical racism than Black students and whether historical knowledge would mediate racial differences in perceptions of isolated and systemic racism.
candidates.citation_sentence: In the two studies reported herein, we attempted to replicate prior research on the Marley hypothesis, which argues that White Americans are more ignorant of historical instances of racism than Black Americans and that this ignorance of history mediates racial differences in perceptions of racism (Bonam et al., 2018, study 1;[13].
candidates.notes: The authors explicitly state that Study 1 failed to replicate prior results: historical knowledge did not differ significantly by race and did not mediate racial differences in perceived racism. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
